Elise Hartmann (1842–1901) worked on her novel Die andere Stadt between 1878 and 1886. In it, industrialization changed a city – and with it the life paths and relationships of its inhabitants. Hartmann began several times new, shifted chapters and let figures disappear. Individual chapters appeared in advance in magazines; the novel remained unfinished and was never published as a book. In the estate there are notebooks, two manuscript convolutes and a revised pure script. Deleted, marginal additions and different pages tell different stories of his origin. Which designs belong together? What was changed when? Miriam Falk's team wants to make these connections visible in a genetic edition and make them comprehensible by the digitized manuscript. The printed volume offers a well-founded reading version and selected variants. Lukas examines the work genealogy; Nora traces how figures and narrative perspectives change. Both work on their own dissertations at the same time. Four years are financed. However, research, publishing sentence and digital publication follow their own timetables.
